title: Returned Service Payments and the Extension Deposit Rate on Vehicle Purchase Agreements
content:
**Credit office guidance, Vehicle Purchase Agreements extension deposits**

Returned payments on the buyer's service account add a returned-payment rate to the extension deposit rate. The count is taken from the service ledger in **Service Accounts and Repair Orders**, using its returned-payment entries: payments by check or by ACH that the bank returned unpaid.

**Rule.**
- Two or more check or ACH payments returned unpaid in the last 24 whole months before the handling date add **2 percent**.
- Exactly one adds **1 percent**.
- None adds nothing.

**What counts.**
- Only service payments made by check or by ACH and returned unpaid are counted. A returned payment of any other kind is not counted.
- A returned payment falls in the last 24 whole months when fewer than 24 whole calendar months have passed from the date its return was received, as shown on the service ledger, to the handling date. A month is whole once the same day of the month is reached.

| Returned check or ACH service payments in the window | Returned-payment rate added |
|---|---|
| 0 | Nothing |
| 1 | 1 percent |
| 2 or more | 2 percent |

**Boundary of the window (hypothetical dates).** Take a handling date of 14 March in some year.
- A return received on 15 March two years earlier is counted. Only 23 whole months have passed, because the 24th month becomes whole on 15 March of the handling year, which is after the handling date.
- A return received on 14 March two years earlier is not counted. Exactly 24 whole months have passed by the handling date.

**Hypothetical illustration.** The service ledger shows one returned ACH payment ten months ago and one returned check payment thirty months ago. Only the ACH return falls in the window, so the rate added is 1 percent.
